title: Carved ash jam spoon
subtitle: A short-handled, wide-bowled spoon for jars and preserve pots
excerpt: A short ash spoon with a broad, flat-bottomed bowl that reaches the sides of a jam jar cleanly. Green ash, axe rough-out, sloyd-knife finish, hook-knife bowl. Food-safe with a raw-linseed cure.
sourceNotes: Cassell's Cyclopaedia of Mechanics vol. III (1885) for the knife-work sequence; traditional UK dairy and preserve spoon patterns from the Museum of English Rural Life open-access collection.

glossaryTerms.definition: Freshly felled or recently riven wood, still high in moisture content. Carves easily under hand tools.
The rough-shaped piece of wood from which the finished item is carved.
A short straight-bladed knife with a stout handle; the Swedish school-craft standard for whittling and spoon-carving.

content.text: A jam spoon is wider than a teaspoon and shorter than a dessert spoon. The bowl is flat-bottomed rather than hemispherical so it reaches the curved base of a jam jar without tilting. The handle is 12 cm long: short enough that the spoon rests across the top of a jar without sliding in. This is a project in
green wood
ash, completed at a beginner's pace in one session.
Before you start cutting.
Grip: four-finger grip on the work; thumb-push grip on the knife. Never make a cut whose blade-path can reach a body part.
Cut direction: push cuts (blade away from body) and thumb-pivot cuts are the default. Pull cuts only with the work braced against the chest and the blade-arc unable to reach anything vital.
Sharpening: a dull tool is more dangerous than a sharp one. The dull tool slips. Strop every fifteen minutes of carving, hone weekly, oilstone monthly.
First aid: keep a styptic pencil, gauze, and a clean dressing within reach. Apply firm pressure, elevate, and dress. A cut that shows fat or won't close with pressure goes to A&E, not a plaster.
Workspace: stable seat, good light, no children or pets within arm-and-blade reach.
Wood
Ash in the green state is the primary recommendation: it is strong in thin sections, which matters for a short handle that will be stressed sideways when scooping from a jar. The
blank

starts at 18 cm long and 6 cm wide. A section split from a log works well; a branch section 6 to 8 cm across also works. Sycamore is the food-safe alternative if ash is unavailable. Both dry pale and flavour-neutral.
Tools
Carving axe: for removing bulk waste to the outline.
Sloyd knife: for all profiling and surface work.
Hook knife, small radius: for the flat-bottomed bowl hollow.
Leather strop: strop every fifteen minutes.
Raw linseed oil: food-safe finish with a two-week cure.
Workspace
A low carving stool and a chopping block. The blank is short enough that it can be held securely in the non-knife hand throughout. Keep the strop on your knee or on a surface within reach.
Method
Step 1: Mark and axe the outline

Draw the spoon from above on the flat split face. The bowl is 7 cm long and 5 cm wide. The handle is 11 cm long, 2 cm wide at the shoulder, 1 cm wide at the tip. Use the carving axe to remove the waste outside the drawn lines. Short, controlled strokes; the blank is small and the axe is sharp.
Step 2: Profile with the sloyd knife
Hold the
blank
with a four-finger grip. Use the
sloyd knife
in push cut to refine the outline and thin the handle. The handle should be 8 mm thick at mid-length: thin enough to sit across a jar rim. The bowl face stays flat at this stage.
Step 3: Hollow the bowl

The bowl of a jam spoon is shallow: 8 mm deep at the centre and nearly flat at the sides. The small hook knife is suited to this work because its tight radius lets you press into the corners of a small bowl oval without the blade tip fouling the rim. Work from the centre out in curving strokes, keeping the cut direction consistent around the oval. The grain of ash runs the length of the blank, so cuts across the bowl go across the grain and may lift slightly; short strokes and a sharp edge prevent tearing.
Step 4: Back of the bowl

Turn the spoon over. Use the sloyd knife in push cuts to dome the underside of the bowl lightly. Because the bowl is shallow, the dome is also shallow: about 5 mm proud of the flat handle plane. Try a cut from bowl shoulder to bowl centre; if the grain lifts, reverse and cut from the opposite rim.
Step 5: Handle tip

Round the end of the handle slightly so it is comfortable to hold. A gentle dome is enough. Sand the tip smooth if you prefer a clean surface for an initials-burned decoration, though the knife finish alone is acceptable.
Finishing

Leave the carved spoon to dry for five to seven days. The small mass of this piece means it dries faster than a large eating spoon. Once dry, apply raw linseed oil, soak for one hour, wipe surplus, and leave for two weeks before food contact.
Variations
Lengthen the handle to 18 cm for a honey-jar spoon with enough reach to stir a deep jar.
Carve a small hole through the tip of the handle so the spoon can hang from a jar rim.
Four spoons in different woods make a good gift. Sycamore, birch, ash, and cherry each take the oil differently and look distinct at the table.
Care

Wash by hand and dry immediately. The short handle goes into a sticky jam pot regularly, which is an ideal environment for bacterial build-up in a crack. Keep the finish in good condition: re-oil when the wood looks dry or after any prolonged contact with water.

attrs.symptom: The bowl has a ridge at the centre
attrs.cause: The hook knife passed the deepest point and left a step where the stroke ended.
attrs.fix: Make the final strokes pass through the centre and out the far rim continuously. Do not stop in the middle of the bowl.

attrs.symptom: The bowl walls are too thin near the rim
attrs.cause: The hook knife angled outward too early on the rim edge.
attrs.fix: Keep the knife perpendicular to the bowl surface for the first few strokes to establish the wall thickness, then angle toward the centre for the final depth.

attrs.symptom: The handle snapped at the bowl shoulder
attrs.cause: The handle was too thin at the shoulder: less than 6 mm in a short-grained species.
attrs.fix: Keep shoulder thickness at 8 mm minimum. The shoulder is the point of highest stress.
